title: Deployment Playbook Schema
description: Machine-readable schema metadata for enterprise deployment playbooks generated by the deployment-playbook skill.

severityLevels.critical: Blocking issue. Document is not fit for operational use.
severityLevels.high: Serious deficiency. Must be corrected before approval or execution.
severityLevels.medium: Important completeness issue. Should be fixed before formal sign-off.
severityLevels.low: Advisory issue. Acceptable temporarily if explicitly risk-accepted.

PLAY-001.title: Document Control block present
PLAY-001.description: The playbook must contain a dedicated Document Control section with core metadata so operators can identify ownership, revision state, and formal governance status.

PLAY-002.title: Playbook ID follows PLY-XXX-NNN format
PLAY-002.description: Each playbook requires a stable identifier in the format PLY-XXX-NNN so it can be referenced in ticketing systems, CAB records, audits, and change calendars.

PLAY-003.title: Version field present and semver format
PLAY-003.description: A version field in semantic version format communicates revision maturity and supports controlled updates during review, approval, and retirement.

PLAY-004.title: Status value is allowed
PLAY-004.description: The status must be one of Draft, In Review, Approved, Active, or Retired so readers know whether the playbook is ready for operational use.

PLAY-005.title: At least one approver listed
PLAY-005.description: Deployment playbooks require accountable approval. At least one named approver must be captured in Document Control or the Approvals section.

PLAY-006.title: Purpose section present
PLAY-006.description: Every playbook must explain why the deployment exists and what business or technical objective it serves.

PLAY-007.title: In-scope and Out-of-scope defined
PLAY-007.description: Clear scope boundaries prevent accidental expansion of the change, reduce coordination failures, and set expectations for stakeholders.

PLAY-008.title: At least one deployment phase defined
PLAY-008.description: A production playbook must break execution into explicit phases so teams can coordinate checkpoints, pauses, and approvals.

PLAY-009.title: Each phase has rollback trigger defined
PLAY-009.description: Rollback conditions must be explicit for every deployment phase so teams know when to stop, reverse, or escalate.

PLAY-010.title: Risk Register table present with at least one entry
PLAY-010.description: A RAID-style risk register is mandatory so deployment risks, owners, and mitigations are reviewed before implementation.

PLAY-011.title: Risk Register has all eight required columns
PLAY-011.description: The risk register must include the standard eight RAID columns so probability, impact, ownership, and status are auditable.

PLAY-012.title: Rollback Strategy section present
PLAY-012.description: Production changes require a dedicated rollback strategy that describes how to recover safely if the deployment fails or degrades service.

PLAY-013.title: Rollback time objective (RTO) defined
PLAY-013.description: Rollback planning must include an RTO or rollback time target so leadership can evaluate exposure and escalation urgency.

PLAY-014.title: Communication Plan table present
PLAY-014.description: Stakeholder communication must be planned with audience, channel, owner, and timing so updates are predictable during the change.

PLAY-015.title: Success Criteria section present
PLAY-015.description: A deployment is not complete until measurable success criteria are defined for functionality, performance, and reliability.

PLAY-016.title: Post-Deployment Validation section present
PLAY-016.description: The playbook must describe how the team verifies the service after rollout and before the change is formally closed.

PLAY-017.title: Contacts & Escalation table present
PLAY-017.description: Operational contacts must be documented so the incident commander or release manager can escalate quickly during execution.

PLAY-018.title: Approvals table present
PLAY-018.description: Formal approval evidence is required for auditability and change governance, especially for normal and emergency changes.

PLAY-019.title: Environment Matrix table present
PLAY-019.description: A deployment playbook must show the environments, regions, tiers, purposes, and deployment order affected by the rollout.

PLAY-020.title: Change Management section with change type defined
PLAY-020.description: The playbook must identify the change type and governance path so change scheduling, CAB involvement, and freeze controls are clear.
